name: Black powder
note: Burns, never detonates: always 'full', its re prices it. Gurney 640 m/s (MSIAC L-295, 90th percentile). Few big slow pieces; the most fires.

name: Wet guncotton
note: Nitrocellulose at 25-30% water (Russia 1890s-1905). Heats and air [EST]: dry NC's less the water. Under-initiated by weak primers: many duds.

name: Lyddite
note: Picric acid (also Melinite). in_plate 0.35 sourced (armor/04 §6, Jutland). Fine splinters.

name: Shimose
note: Picric acid undiluted, lacquer and wax lined (Japan). Bore prematures and bursts on the water are 12's hidden stats, not modelled.

name: TNT
note: Trotyl, Fp 02. Heats measured (LLNL 4.57, 14.96 MJ/kg), Gurney IATG 01.80. Needs a strong booster.

name: TNT/wax
note: TNT with ~10% wax (Germany's Fp 5-20, the RN's post-war TNT/beeswax). Heats and air [EST]: TNT's with the wax's combustion.

name: Explosive D
note: Ammonium picrate (Dunnite, USN). re [EST, unsourced]; 11 has 0.90. The most impact-insensitive filler in quantity.

name: Shellite
note: Picric acid with dinitrophenol (RN Greenboy on). Full 0.90 with CE sourced; low-order without it until the late 1920s.

name: TNA
note: Trinitroanisole, Type 91 bakuyaku (IJN). re [EST, unsourced]. Needed a liner of 1/3-1/2 of the cavity.

name: Amatol 60/40
note: TNT 60, ammonium nitrate 40: the shortage filler. Heats and air [EST] between TNT and 80/20.

name: Amatol 80/20
note: Ammonium nitrate 80, TNT 20: about five times the shells per ton of TNT. Oxygen-balanced: no afterburn. Brisance 0.62 from NOL's fragments.

name: RDX/TNT
note: Late-war HE (the RN's 15" HE Mk VII TNT/RDX). Gurney, brisance, in_plate and full [EST]; too sensitive for AP unless phlegmatised.

name: Comp B
note: RDX 60, TNT 40. Gurney 2,774 and brisance 1.41 (IATG) sourced; heats [EST] as RDX/TNT.
